# Ecclesiastes Chapter 6 -- The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**6:1** There-is an-evil [ra'ah] that I-saw under the-sun, and-it [is] great [rabbah] upon the-human [ha-adam]:

**6:2** A-man [ish] to-whom God gives riches [osher] and-possessions [nekhasim] and-honor [kavod], and-there-is-nothing lacking [einennu chaser] to-his-soul [le-nafsho] from-all that he-desires [yit'avveh], but-God does-not-empower-him [lo yashlitennu ha-Elohim] to-eat [le'ekhol] from-it, for a-foreign [nokhri] man eats-it. This [is] vapor [havel] and-an-evil [ra] sickness [choli] it [is].

**6:3** If a-man begets [yolid] a-hundred [me'ah] and-lives [yichyeh] many [rabboth] years, and-much [rav] are the-days of-his-years, but-his-soul [nafsho] is-not-satisfied [lo tisba] from the-good [min-ha-tovah], and-also burial [qevurah] there-is-not [lo haytah] to-him — I-say [amarti] [that] better [tov] than-him [mimmennu] [is] the-stillborn [ha-nefel].

**6:4** For in-vapor [ba-hevel] it-comes [ba] and-in-darkness [ba-choshekh] it-goes [yelekh], and-in-darkness its-name [shemo] is-covered [yekhusse]. **6:5** Also the-sun [shemesh] it-has-not-seen [lo ra'ah] and-has-not-known [ve-lo yada]; rest [nachat] to-this [la-zeh] more-than-to-that [mi-zeh].

**6:6** And-even-if [ve-illu] he-lived [chayah] a-thousand [elef] years twice [pe'amayim] and-good [tovah] he-has-not-seen [lo ra'ah] — does-not the-all [ha-kol] go to one place [maqom echad]?

**6:7** All the-toil [amal] of-the-human [ha-adam] [is] for-his-mouth [le-fihu], and-yet the-appetite [ha-nefesh] is-not-filled [lo timmale'].

**6:8** For what advantage [mah-yoter] [has] the-wise [le-chakham] over the-fool [min-ha-kesil]? What [advantage has] the-poor-one [le-ani] who-knows [yode'a] to-walk before the-living [neged ha-chayyim]?

**6:9** Better [tov] [is] the-sight [mar'eh] of-the-eyes [einayim] than-the-wandering [me-halakh] of-the-appetite [nefesh]. Also this [is] vapor [havel] and-striving-after [re'ut] wind [ruach].

**6:10** What has-been [mah she-hayah], already [kevar] its-name has-been-called [niqra shemo], and-it-is-known [ve-noda] that-he [is] human [adam]; and-he-is-not-able [ve-lo yukhal] to-contend [la-din] with the-one-who [im she-] is-mightier [taqif] than-him [mimmennu].

**6:11** For there-are many [harbeh] words [devarim] that-increase [marbim] vapor [havel]; what advantage [mah-yoter] [is there] to-the-human [la-adam]?

**6:12** For who knows [mi yode'a] what [is] good for-the-human [la-adam] in-life [ba-chayyim], [in] the-counted days [mispar yemei] of-his-vapor-life [chayyei hevlo], and-he-makes-them [ve-ya'asem] like-a-shadow [ka-tzel]? For who can-tell [yaggid] to-the-human [la-adam] what will-be after-him [acharav] under the-sun?

---

## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.2 — "a foreign man eats it":** The Hebrew *ish nokhri* (a stranger/foreigner) receives what the wealthy man cannot enjoy. The tragedy is not poverty but the disconnect between having and enjoying. This is the dark mirror of 5:19 — where God gives the power to enjoy, here God withholds it.

**v.3 — "the stillborn":** The Hebrew *nefel* refers to a miscarried or stillborn child. Qohelet's shocking comparison — that a stillborn is better off than someone who has everything but cannot enjoy it — is the most extreme statement in the book about the centrality of enjoyment.

**v.12 — "his vapor-life" (chayyei hevlo):** EMET preserves the compound *chayyei hevlo* — literally "the life of his vapor." Life itself is described as belonging to vapor, not merely accompanied by it. This is Qohelet's most condensed statement of the human condition.

*-- EMET*
